themes.label: Mind & Words
themes.blurb: Where you talk yourself out of feeling, or talk over what's true.

prompts.prompt: Which emotions do I find hardest to put into words?
prompts.followUp: When I can't name what I'm feeling, what do I do instead — go quiet, get sarcastic, change the subject, overexplain?

prompts.prompt: What did I say today that I didn't mean?
prompts.followUp: Was it to spare someone, or to spare myself the conversation honesty would have started?

prompts.prompt: Which subject do I reliably change when it comes up?
prompts.followUp: What happens in my body in the half-second before I change it?

prompts.prompt: What truth about myself do I avoid saying out loud, even to people I trust?
prompts.followUp: If I said it anyway, right now, what's the worst thing I imagine would happen — and how likely is that, really?

prompts.prompt: How do I use overthinking to avoid actually feeling something?
prompts.followUp: What would happen if, just once, I let the feeling move through me before I tried to analyze it?

prompts.prompt: Whose voice is narrating when I talk to myself about my own failures?
prompts.followUp: Would I let that person speak that way to someone I love, in front of me?

prompts.prompt: What story about my life have I told so often, and so well, that I no longer know how much of it is true?
prompts.followUp: Who does that version protect — and what would I have to admit if I stopped telling it?

prompts.prompt: Where do I use being articulate as a weapon — winning the conversation instead of being honest in it?
prompts.followUp: Name the last person I out-talked rather than listened to. What were they actually trying to say?

prompts.prompt: What am I lying about right now, in a way I've decided doesn't count?
prompts.followUp: What makes it not count — and would I accept that same reasoning from someone who lied to me that way?

themes.label: Worth & Love
themes.blurb: Where love, money, and self-worth get tangled into one fear.

prompts.prompt: How do I seek validation from others, and what would it take to give that to myself instead?
prompts.followUp: What's one thing I did well this week that I haven't told anyone, because I was waiting for someone else to notice first?

prompts.prompt: How do I handle rejection, and what does my reaction say about how I see my own worth?
prompts.followUp: If a friend described being rejected the way I just described it, would I tell them it meant the same thing about their worth?

prompts.prompt: What do I do with my body and my face when someone compliments me?
prompts.followUp: What would it take to just say thank you and let it land?

prompts.prompt: What fears stop me from fully letting someone love me?
prompts.followUp: Whose love, growing up, came with conditions — and am I still meeting those same conditions for people now?

prompts.prompt: What am I still doing to earn love that I was never supposed to have to earn?
prompts.followUp: Who set that price — and have I ever tested whether anyone still charges it?

prompts.prompt: Who gets the version of me that's easiest to love, rather than the real one?
prompts.followUp: What do I believe would happen to us if I stopped managing their impression of me?

prompts.prompt: Who do I keep in my life because being needed by them is easier than being known by anyone?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to feel, in the quiet, if that relationship ended tomorrow?

prompts.prompt: What have I accepted from someone because I decided, somewhere along the way, that it was the most I deserved?
prompts.followUp: When did I decide that — and what would it cost me to find out I was wrong?

prompts.prompt: Where am I withholding love as a form of control, and calling it something more respectable?
prompts.followUp: What am I actually trying to make them understand — and why won't I just say it?

themes.label: Anger & Drive
themes.blurb: Where action turns into self-sabotage, or anger turns inward.

prompts.prompt: What tends to trigger my temper fastest, and what is usually underneath the anger?
prompts.followUp: The last time I snapped at someone, what was I actually afraid of in that moment?

prompts.prompt: How do I tend to avoid discomfort, and what might happen if I moved straight through it instead of around it?
prompts.followUp: What's one uncomfortable conversation or task I've been circling for weeks — and what's the smallest first step toward it?

prompts.prompt: What irritated me today that was, objectively, very small?
prompts.followUp: What was already sitting in me before that thing happened?

prompts.prompt: How do I sabotage my own success, and why might I be doing this?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to risk losing if I actually let myself succeed without sabotaging it?

prompts.prompt: Who am I angry at that I have never told?
prompts.followUp: What do I do with that anger instead — and who tends to catch it in their place?

prompts.prompt: What am I punishing myself for in ways I'd call discipline if anyone asked?
prompts.followUp: If someone else set those same rules for me, would I call it discipline or cruelty?

prompts.prompt: Who have I hurt and never made right, because apologising would mean admitting I'm capable of that?
prompts.followUp: What has my silence cost them, in all the time I've spent protecting my own self-image?

prompts.prompt: What am I refusing to do — right now, this month — that I know would change things?
prompts.followUp: Is it easier to be someone with potential than someone with results? Answer that honestly.

prompts.prompt: Where is my anger actually correct, and what would I have to change if I let myself take it seriously?
prompts.followUp: What have I dismissed as overreacting that was really just accurate?

themes.label: Belief & Expansion
themes.blurb: Where limiting beliefs and overpromising both come from the same fear of not enough.

prompts.prompt: When I think about my future, what fears come up most frequently?
prompts.followUp: If that fear came true tomorrow, what is the very first thing I would actually do?

prompts.prompt: What did I say yes to this week that I wanted to decline?
prompts.followUp: What did I imagine would happen if I'd simply said no?

prompts.prompt: What am I waiting for before I let my real life start?
prompts.followUp: What would today look like if that thing never arrives?

prompts.prompt: What limiting beliefs are holding me back from the life I actually want?
prompts.followUp: Where did I first learn to believe that — and whose voice does it sound like?

prompts.prompt: Where in my life do I overpromise or overcommit, and what am I trying to prove when I do?
prompts.followUp: What would it feel like to disappoint someone by simply telling them the truth up front?

prompts.prompt: What do I believe about how the world works that I have never once tested?
prompts.followUp: Who benefits from me continuing to believe it?

prompts.prompt: What have I been calling faith, or timing, or optimism, that is actually avoidance of one specific decision?
prompts.followUp: What is the decision — and what has not making it already cost me?

prompts.prompt: If I never become the person I keep saying I'm going to become, what will I have spent this life doing instead?
prompts.followUp: Is that sentence uncomfortable because it's unfair, or because it's accurate?

prompts.prompt: Whose life am I quietly measuring mine against?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to feel if I admitted I want what they have — and what does wanting it say about me that I've decided is unacceptable?

themes.label: Inner Critic & Limits
themes.blurb: Where the inner critic enforces rules that were never really yours to keep.

prompts.prompt: How do I react when someone criticizes me, and what does that reaction protect?
prompts.followUp: What's the difference between criticism that's actually useful and criticism that just confirms what I already feared about myself?

prompts.prompt: What did I criticise myself for today?
prompts.followUp: Would I even have noticed if someone else had done the same thing?

prompts.prompt: What rule am I following today that nobody actually gave me?
prompts.followUp: What do I imagine happens if I break it once?

prompts.prompt: What does my inner critic say to me most often, and whose voice does it actually sound like?
prompts.followUp: If I spoke to myself the way I speak to someone I love, what would today's inner monologue sound like instead?

prompts.prompt: What boundaries do I struggle to maintain, and what am I afraid will happen if I hold them?
prompts.followUp: Who in my life reacts the worst when I do hold a boundary — and what does their reaction usually talk me into doing?

prompts.prompt: What am I proud of that I've never let myself enjoy?
prompts.followUp: What did I move on to before the feeling could land — and why does resting feel unsafe?

prompts.prompt: Whose approval am I still working for — including people who are gone, or who were never going to give it?
prompts.followUp: What would I do with the hours and the energy if I stopped?

prompts.prompt: What have I not forgiven myself for, and what does holding onto it let me avoid doing next?
prompts.followUp: If I set it down, what would I no longer have an excuse not to attempt?

prompts.prompt: Where have I mistaken self-punishment for self-improvement, and how many years have I spent inside that mistake?
prompts.followUp: Measured honestly: what has it actually produced, and what has it cost?

themes.label: Detachment & Independence
themes.blurb: Where independence turns into a wall instead of a strength.

prompts.prompt: Which of my personality traits do I try to hide from others, and what would happen if I didn't?
prompts.followUp: Who has earned the right to see the version of me I usually keep hidden — and have I let them?

prompts.prompt: When did I last say “I'm fine” and not mean it?
prompts.followUp: What would I have said instead, if the person had asked twice?

prompts.prompt: What did I turn down this week that I actually wanted?
prompts.followUp: What reason did I give, and what was the real one?

prompts.prompt: Do I use independence to avoid needing people, and if so, what am I protecting myself from?
prompts.followUp: What's one small thing I could ask for help with this week, just to practice being needed without it costing me anything?

prompts.prompt: When do I retreat into logic or distance instead of staying present with how I actually feel?
prompts.followUp: What feeling was I avoiding the last time I told myself 'it's fine, it doesn't matter'?

prompts.prompt: What do I get out of being the one who doesn't need anyone?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to feel if I let someone close enough to disappoint me?

prompts.prompt: Who have I left before they could leave me, and told myself it was because I'd outgrown them?
prompts.followUp: What did I actually feel in the week after — and did I let myself feel it, or did I get busy?

prompts.prompt: Which relationships have I ended by simply going quiet, rather than saying the true thing?
prompts.followUp: What did that leave them holding — and do I know, or have I made a point of never finding out?

prompts.prompt: If I'm so independent, why does being genuinely known still feel more dangerous than being alone?
prompts.followUp: What do I believe someone would find, if they got all the way in?

themes.label: Illusion & Letting Go
themes.blurb: Where denial, escapism, and old grudges all serve the same purpose: avoiding what's real.

prompts.prompt: How do I escape from feelings I don't want to deal with — distraction, fantasy, substances, scrolling?
prompts.followUp: What is usually waiting underneath, in the ten minutes right before I reach for the escape?

prompts.prompt: What did I reach for tonight — the phone, the drink, the next episode — and what was happening right before?
prompts.followUp: What was the feeling I was about ten minutes away from having?

prompts.prompt: What am I pretending not to know?
prompts.followUp: How long have I known it?

prompts.prompt: What aspects of myself am I in denial about, and how can I start to confront them honestly?
prompts.followUp: If a close friend named this thing about me out loud, would I feel exposed, relieved, or both — and why?

prompts.prompt: What grudges am I still holding onto, and how are they actually serving me?
prompts.followUp: What would I lose, besides the grudge itself, if I let this one go today?

prompts.prompt: Which version of a person am I actually in a relationship with — them, or my idea of them?
prompts.followUp: What do I do with the evidence that doesn't fit the idea?

prompts.prompt: What have I dressed up as forgiveness that is really just my unwillingness to have the conversation?
prompts.followUp: Who does that protect — and what is still unsaid between us?

prompts.prompt: What am I grieving that I have never once called grief?
prompts.followUp: What have I called it instead, and how has that name kept me from putting it down?

prompts.prompt: Where am I the villain in someone else's honest account of what happened?
prompts.followUp: Write their version, in their words, without defending myself once. What's hardest to leave in?

themes.label: Power & the Unconscious
themes.blurb: Where control, secrecy, and shame guard the parts of you that feel most dangerous to show.

prompts.prompt: What am I keeping private today that isn't really a secret?
prompts.followUp: What would change if exactly one person knew it?

prompts.prompt: Where did I try to control something small today?
prompts.followUp: What was the uncertainty underneath it?

prompts.prompt: Who am I envious of right now?
prompts.followUp: What does the envy tell me I want, but haven't admitted to wanting?

prompts.prompt: What part of myself am I most ashamed of, and how can I learn to accept it?
prompts.followUp: If that part of me were a person, what would it need to hear to finally feel safe?

prompts.prompt: In which areas of my life do I feel powerless, and what would it look like to reclaim even a small piece of that power?
prompts.followUp: Who or what currently holds the power I wish I had in that area — and how did they end up holding it?

prompts.prompt: How does my shadow self show up when I'm under stress — controlling, secretive, jealous, withdrawn?
prompts.followUp: What was the very first situation, even far back in childhood, where that reaction kept me safe?

prompts.prompt: What do I get out of the situation I keep describing as something being done to me?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to give up if it resolved tomorrow — and is any part of me relieved that it hasn't?

prompts.prompt: What is the thing about me that I believe would end how people see me, if it were widely known?
prompts.followUp: Is it genuinely unforgivable, or has it just never been examined in daylight?

prompts.prompt: Where do I use other people's need for me as leverage, without ever calling it leverage?
prompts.followUp: What am I afraid would happen if they stopped needing me?

themes.label: Feeling & Roots
themes.blurb: Where childhood patterns still decide how safe vulnerability feels today.

prompts.prompt: When was the last time I felt truly vulnerable, and what did that moment teach me?
prompts.followUp: Did I let anyone see that vulnerability, or did I process it entirely alone — and why?

prompts.prompt: What did I feel today that I didn't have time for?
prompts.followUp: Where did it go?

prompts.prompt: Who did I want to reach out to today, and didn't?
prompts.followUp: What stopped me?

prompts.prompt: What childhood wounds am I still carrying, and how do they show up in my closest relationships today?
prompts.followUp: What did I need to hear back then that nobody said — and could I say it to myself now?

prompts.prompt: Where do I over-give or over-protect the people I love, and what am I afraid would happen if I stopped?
prompts.followUp: What does it cost me, physically and emotionally, to keep giving past the point I actually have left to give?

prompts.prompt: What role did I play in my family, and who am I when I'm not playing it?
prompts.followUp: When did I last get to find out?

prompts.prompt: What did my parents do that I swore I would never do — and where have I done it anyway?
prompts.followUp: Who has been on the receiving end, and have I ever acknowledged it to them?

prompts.prompt: What did I need as a child that I am still, at this age, trying to get from people who cannot give it?
prompts.followUp: What would it mean to stop asking them, and to grieve that instead of continuing the campaign?

prompts.prompt: Whose love have I been performing for in a way that has quietly shaped every major decision I've made?
prompts.followUp: Which decision would look different if I had made it purely for myself?

themes.label: Pride & Visibility
themes.blurb: Where the need to be admired covers for the fear of being ordinary, or wrong.

prompts.prompt: How do I react when I'm not the center of attention, and what does that reaction protect?
prompts.followUp: What would it feel like to do something well and tell absolutely no one?

prompts.prompt: What did I do today mainly so that someone would see it?
prompts.followUp: Would I have done it at all if no one could?

prompts.prompt: When was I last genuinely happy for someone whose win I wanted?
prompts.followUp: What did I say out loud, and what did I actually feel?

prompts.prompt: What is something I find almost impossible to admit I was wrong about?
prompts.followUp: What do I imagine people would think of me if I admitted that mistake out loud?

prompts.prompt: Where in my life am I performing confidence instead of actually feeling it?
prompts.followUp: Who in my life has earned the right to see me uncertain, and when did I last let them?

prompts.prompt: What do I want to be known for — and what am I actually known for?
prompts.followUp: What is the gap made of?

prompts.prompt: What am I still doing purely because stopping would mean admitting the last several years went into the wrong thing?
prompts.followUp: How much longer am I willing to pay that, just to avoid saying it out loud?

prompts.prompt: Who have I made smaller so that I could feel large — and would they recognise my account of it?
prompts.followUp: What would I have to feel about myself to put that right?

prompts.prompt: If nobody ever found out about anything I achieve from here on, would I still want the life I'm building?
prompts.followUp: Which parts fall away in that version — and what does that tell me about who I've been building it for?

1: Where do I feel this in my body right now — tight chest, clenched jaw, heavy stomach? Just notice, no need to fix it.
What is one small, low-stakes way I could respond differently the next time this exact pattern shows up?
What's one tiny act of self-trust I can offer myself today, in spite of all of this?
2: If I spoke to this part of myself with the same compassion I'd offer a close friend, what would I say?
What would it cost me to keep carrying this — and what might it free up if I set it down, even partially?
Whose voice does the harshest part of this story sound like — and is it actually mine?
What part of this is genuinely mine to carry, and what part did I pick up from someone else and never put down?
3: Read back what I just wrote as though a friend had handed it to me. What is the first thing I'd want them to know?
Where did I stop writing? That stopping point is usually the actual thing — what is sitting just past it?
If this is true, what does it ask of me — and just as importantly, what does it not ask of me? Separating those keeps this from becoming one more way to punish myself.
What is the smallest true thing here that I could act on this week — not solve, not fix, just act on?
Who would have to know this for it to stop being a private weight? Do I want that yet? “Not yet” is a real answer.
Nothing I found here is news to the part of me that has been carrying it. What would it mean to stop making that part carry it alone?

depths.label: Opening
depths.blurb: A way in. Answerable in a few minutes, on an ordinary day.

depths.label: Deeper
depths.blurb: Asks you to name a pattern rather than an incident.

depths.label: Unflinching
depths.blurb: Hard questions with no comfortable exit. Give these time, and privacy.
